value.rationale: The source identifies a physically and dynamically motivated high-frequency probability question but gives only an upper bound and a mean zero count. The new result computes the universal leading event probability for all Fourier cutoffs, even degree growing with frequency, and proves that rare events yield exactly two rather than arbitrarily many transverse Melnikov roots. This distinction matters for understanding the geometry of first-order homoclinic splitting and is not an unmotivated parameter substitution.
